extracted.intended_audience: screenwriters / scriptwriters and filmmakers (aspiring and professional) looking to build beat sheets and step-outlines
extracted.subtask_description: Using an online outliner to build a beat sheet and step-outline for film or TV scripts, choosing from multiple story-structure templates and exporting the outline to a screenplay-first-draft workflow (including speech-to-screenplay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeform
rubrics_metrics.description: No guide…Outline by the seat of your pants. But still, it’s an outline!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want an unstructured, organic approach to mapping beats; allows flexibility instead of enforcing predefined plot points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save the Cat
rubrics_metrics.description: Blake Snyder’s Hollywood method defines the key plot points and when they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Save the Cat to position standard industry beats and timing (e.g., opening image, catalyst, midpoint, finale). Useful for commercial Hollywood-style scripts that follow recognizable beat timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4 Act Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The classic Four-Act Structure outlines the setup, the rise / fall, and resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to break a feature into setup, escalating conflict, low point, and resolution; suitable for pacing that emphasizes a clear rise/fall arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8 Sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A structure that generates cliffhangers and twists from AFI & USC film schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide the story into eight sequences to create built-in mini-arcs and frequent cliffhangers—often taught in film school for momentum and turning points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Circle
rubrics_metrics.description: Dan Harmon’s hero’s journey for sitcoms and ‘there-and-back-again’ stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Harmon’s circle to map a character’s transformation through stages (comfort → need → search → find → take → return, etc.), particularly useful for episodic sitcom structure and character-centered arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Act TV
rubrics_metrics.description: Freytag’s theater structure was adapted to shape hour-long TV with teasers and tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when structuring hour-long television episodes with acts/teasers/tags to satisfy broadcast pacing and commercial break beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9Cs
rubrics_metrics.description: A beatsheet with a strong spine that balances the inner & outer journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 9Cs beatsheet to ensure both plot-level (outer) events and character/internal (inner) arcs are balanced throughout the outline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pixar (story spine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pixar’s “Once upon a time…” story spine guides how they break story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Pixar spine pattern (simple, clear inciting incidents and consequence-driven beats) to craft emotionally clear and tightly structured narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syd Field
rubrics_metrics.description: The popular Hollywood form builds toward story pinch points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Syd Field’s paradigm (three-act emphasis with plot points/pinch points) to place turning points and escalate stakes; noted on the page as 'coming soon'—implementation may be forthcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat sheet & step-outline creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Build your beat sheet & step-outline in your browser. Then export it for free into Final Draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a beat-level map and convert it to a step-outline inside the tool; the workflow supports exporting the outline into Final Draft to move from outline to formatted screenplay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talking Draft / Speech-to-Screenplay zero draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Take your step-outline and use our TalkingDraft speech-to-script to produce a first draft faster than you ever imagined! 'Outline… Then “Talk Your Draft”' and 'Your Speech-To-Screenplay Zero Draft'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After outlining, use the Talking Draft speech-to-screenplay method to generate a rapid zero draft by speaking the script; intended as a fast first-draft generation technique that leverages spoken input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free to use / free sign-up
rubrics_metrics.description: FREE TO USE / Free Sign up today! Join Now and Enjoy TalkingDraft for Free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost/accessibility criterion: the tool and TalkingDraft service are presented as free to use, which affects adoption decisions but not the outline content itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility & security
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational criteria: the outliner exports to common apps (e.g., Final Draft) and claims strict security—considerations for workflow integration and protecting drafts.
